$comment: Machine-readable registry of APR test suites and spec-requirement coverage. Verified by scripts/check-test-registry.py, which fails if a referenced fixture or test no longer exists, or if a requirement has no entry. The registry is a claim about coverage; the verifier is what makes the claim checkable. Its v1 requirements remain historical beta.3 coverage while beta.6 migration coverage is added separately.

activeMigrationTarget.coverageStatus: gated; paired representations and streams, semantic digests/manifests, CMS and unsupported proofs, fields scope, witness chains, changed forms, malformed representations, and shipped beta.6 examples are covered

gateStrength.gated: A test fails in CI if the rule is violated. The only level that actually holds an implementation.
gateStrength.partial: Some aspect of the rule is gated; other aspects are not.
gateStrength.indirect: Covered only through another component, not at this rule's own level.
gateStrength.external: Gated by a third-party suite this project does not maintain.
gateStrength.none: No test would fail if the rule were broken.
gateStrength.informative: Not a testable rule — definitional or explanatory text.

dimensions.completeness: Does the component do everything it claims?
dimensions.conformance: Does it agree with the format? (corpus + schema gates)
dimensions.correctness: Does it give right answers? (unit tests + coverage gate)
dimensions.robustness: Does it survive bad input and stay fixed? (edge cases, fuzz, mutation, regression)

suites.gate: schema agrees with every corpus fixture
suites.notes: Deliberately uses no .NET, so it fails the way a third-party SDK would.

suites.gate: ratcheting coverage (a floor, not a bar)
suites.robustnessNotes: CliRobustnessTests points empty, truncated, non-JSON, UTF-16, 50k-nested, binary and wrong-shape files at validate/info/stats. Contract: non-zero exit, no throw, no stack trace in output. Found that `info` exited 0 on any JSON object at all.

suites.notes: GUI suite runs (issue #30 fixed). Conformance is direct rather than inherited, and the project is now inside a coverage gate for the first time - it was excluded entirely while its GUI tests could not run, so there was nothing meaningful to measure. No tests are skipped anywhere in the solution.
AT-SPI smoke test is manual, outside CI. No tests are skipped anywhere in the solution.
The only third-party conformance check in the project.

suites.gate: every shipped beta.6 example must satisfy the published schema and beta.6 parser gate
suites.notes: All 19 real form files - SF-86, IRS 990, IRS 1040, W-4, the bundled starter templates and two importer outputs. Enumerated from disk, so a new file is covered without being listed anywhere. The conformance corpus is synthetic by design, one rule per fixture; these catch what only shows up at the size and messiness of a real form. Found a shipped example that failed our own validator, and the editor bug that produced it.

suites.gate: processability findings, form-vs-template comparison, and the CLI exit-code contract (0 process / 2 route to a human / 1 unreadable)
suites.notes: Implements specification 6.2 warnings as a receiver-facing report, plus a comparison against the claimed template. Covers the case no response-level check can: a prompt keeping its id while its label changes, so a pipeline files a truthful answer under a question nobody asked.

suites.gate: each workflow the GUI supports, carried start to finish through real files on disk and reloaded to check what was actually written
suites.notes: The suite had deep per-command coverage and a driver that activates every control, but nothing carried a task from beginning to end. These author a template, fill one, edit a saved form, build and fill a table, undo/redo a whole session, fill one party’s share of a multi-party form, walk the wizard, and export a fillable PDF. Partial on completeness: signing and PDF import journeys are still covered only per command.

suites.gate: the shared conformance corpus plus APR CEL binding tests in a locked uv environment
suites.notes: Locked with uv and corpus-gated. Evaluates APR CEL bindings; signatures remain opaque and unchecked.

suites.gate: npm ci && npm test: valid, invalid, malformed, unknown-member, expression-preservation, signature-preservation, and exact-response corpus coverage
suites.notes: Evaluates APR CEL bindings for numeric, boolean, string, list, and dynamic date/time values; signatures remain preserved but unchecked.

suites.gate: npm ci && npm test: semantic order, widget mapping, escaping, accessible help, unknown-type fallback, bidi isolation, and no-network rendering
suites.notes: The renderer is an optional host package, not part of the format-only core. Browser-extension tests are added when that product exists.

suites.gate: npm ci && npm test: local load, safe render, response update, and APRF download workflow
suites.notes: The demo is intentionally local-only: it does not upload a document or follow submission URLs.

suites.gate: the shared valid, invalid, and malformed corpus under Java 21
suites.notes: Project-local Maven wrapper resolves official CEL-Java. Expressions are evaluated; signatures remain preserved but unchecked.

suites.note: Fifteen renderer cases scored by scripts/run-renderer-conformance.py, answered by four drivers — a reference renderer, the TypeScript HTML renderer, the Avalonia desktop client and the PDF exporter — with scripts/check-renderer-teeth.py proving the scorer fails a broken renderer. Reaches the rules no document vector can.

testKinds.notes: veraPDF for PDF/A; cel-spec's suite available for the expression language now that CEL is adopted.

In-process automation-tree assertions run headlessly (AutomationTreeTests). External AT-SPI verification against a live application is still the manual script at tests/at-spi/run_at_spi_smoke.sh, outside CI. Two stubs that claimed to cover this were removed rather than left permanently skipped - a skip hides a gap instead of recording it.
Stryker.NET reports Killed:0. Until it runs, line coverage remains an incomplete behavior-quality signal.

Deterministic mutation fuzzing of the parser (ParserFuzzTests): every truncation and 200 seeded single-character corruptions per corpus fixture, plus hand-built exhaustion structures. Fixed seed so a failure reproduces. Not coverage-guided - a real fuzzer (SharpFuzz) would explore further.
Vision targets 1000+ prompts under 1s; largest fixture is 20.
Requires two conformant implementations; only one exists.

requirements.statement: Advisory feedback never blocks saving, input, or declares a document invalid
requirements.gap: APR-VAL-006 and 033 are renderer obligations: a warning never prevents saving, and never prevents entering text. A document is valid either way, so no document case distinguishes a renderer that blocks the keyboard from one that does not; the renderer suite asks the saving half. APR-VAL-034 is a permission.

requirements.statement: A reported advisory condition carries the code the warnings table names
requirements.gap: APR-VAL-036, 037 and 038 name the codes for the hidden-character conditions chapter 8 states, so that a suite case has a code to ask for. No reader emits them yet: Python, TypeScript and .NET report a fixed list of code points under their own spellings, and Java and the reference validator report nothing (#506, #507, #508). No case scores them until the readers are aligned to the floor, and none is written here because it would fail every driver.

requirements.statement: A parse failure is reported as PARSE_ERROR, outside the exhaustive error table
Any string is a valid response, whatever the hint asked for
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-127 states a floor on what an implementation must accept, not a property of any one document, so no conformance case can carry it: a vector proving a mebibyte is readable would be a mebibyte long. The .NET test that proved it is not in this change, which is specification-only.

requirements.statement: Attestation record members, their presence and domains, closed sub-objects, extension members that round-trip, and a subject resolved by digest alone
requirements.gap: APR-ATTEST-017: the SDK tests resolve an attestation that precedes its subject by digest, so stream position is checked, but no test gives a filename or document id that disagrees with the digest (#333). A missing member is REQUIRED_FIELD by section 7.1, and the .NET reader reports several as WRONG_TYPE (#517), so the examples show absence with `scope` alone.

requirements.statement: A fields scope binds the question and its context, not only the answer; a changed form leaves a fields attestation unresolved, never invalid
requirements.gap: APR-ATTEST-005 has a satisfying example and corpus vector but no violating one: no validator checks what a fields manifest includes. APR-ATTEST-006, 015, 016 and 032 are about what a verifier reports, and the harness scores documents rather than verification reports (#333).

requirements.statement: Authoring data may be held to stricter rules, and no attestation binds a deceptive submission URL
An implementation never Unicode-normalizes authoring data or removes a code point from it
requirements.gap: No case checks it, and the Python and TypeScript SDKs break it: they normalize and strip hint and role text when they read it (#412).

requirements.statement: A validator warns on a submission URL carrying a code point the floor excludes
requirements.gap: Only .NET reports it, as SUBMISSION_URL_HIDDEN_CHARS, a code the warnings table does not name (#507).

requirements.statement: A validator warns on an id outside [A-Za-z0-9_.-]
requirements.gap: No implementation reports it, and the warnings table names no code for it (#508).

requirements.statement: Human-facing text meets the NFC and code point floor, a validator reports a violation, and confusable detection is recommended
A changed form is a new subject; earlier attestations do not transfer; a reader accepts several attestations of one form and an attestation before its subject
requirements.gap: APR-ATTEST-009, that an earlier attestation is never transferred to a changed form, is verifier behaviour: the document is valid either way, and what differs is what a verifier says about it. APR-ATTEST-020, that a verifier holding a form which is not the subject says so alongside `unresolved`, is unreachable for the same reason and additionally needs the harness to score what a verifier reports (#333).

requirements.statement: jcs-sha256 over the semantic model; manifests hold no plaintext; manifest entries are ordered and duplicate-free, carry the root pointer, and bound what a verifier may report; jcs-sha256 is computed over the JCS encoding of the semantic model, never over source syntax
requirements.gap: Entry ordering, the root pointer and the digest shape are checked by the reference validator. No vector asserts APR-DIGEST-005 or 007, which are verifier behaviour, or 010, the completeness of a manifest's entries. APR-DIGEST-008 and 009 have no violating example because the .NET reader reports a manifest entry missing `path` or `digest` as WRONG_TYPE rather than REQUIRED_FIELD (#517).

requirements.statement: A renderer may add layout to an export and never writes it back into the document
The read-only activation and its reserved names; an expression sees the activation and nothing else; an id that is not a CEL identifier is unreachable
requirements.gap: The Java SDK does not bind _now (#513), so no example requires APR-EXPR-020. Every other name in the activation is shown by an example all five implementations evaluate alike.

requirements.statement: A response binds to the CEL type its expectedDataType row gives
requirements.gap: The Python SDK does not bind a boolean response (#512), so no example requires APR-EXPR-024. The multichoice example uses the canonical newline form, since the reference evaluator does not bind the comma-and-space read form (#515).

requirements.statement: Expressions are type-checked at authoring time
requirements.gap: A SHOULD about type-checking at authoring time, before a filler ever sees the form. The harness evaluates a completed document and has no authoring step.

requirements.statement: A result is written in its canonical form, and a failed hint applies its fallback
requirements.gap: No SDK driver reports exprExpected or exprReadOnly results (#514), so no case requires APR-EXPR-030 or 031.

requirements.statement: exprValue marks provenance and never overwrites an unmarked non-empty response
A reader may replace a response it computed itself in the same session
requirements.gap: A permission about a reader's own session state, which the document never records.

requirements.statement: ctx carries host-supplied data and never carries secrets or authorization decisions; a computed prompt stays editable
requirements.gap: APR-EXPR-007 binds a host, and a document cannot show what a host placed in ctx. APR-EXPR-014, that a computed prompt stays editable, is scored by the renderer case a-computed-prompt-stays-editable.

requirements.statement: Expressions are pure, never authoritative over a response, and fail data-preservingly
requirements.gap: APR-EXPR-001 and APR-EXPR-003 are covered by evaluation vectors. APR-EXPR-002, that evaluation is pure and exposes no filesystem, network, process, clock or randomness, cannot be reached by one: a document cannot ask for a capability the language does not have, and proving absence needs inspection of the host rather than a case.

requirements.statement: Expressions are CEL as cel-spec v0.25.3 defines it, with the standard library and standard macros, and no extension library
Evaluation terminates and a reached bound applies the hint fallback
requirements.gap: Degradation on failure is gated. Exact bounds are implementation-defined in this baseline, so no vector asserts a limit.

requirements.statement: An unconvertible response is unbound, never defaulted
Unknown members round-trip and enter whole-document digests; unprefixed names are reserved, extensions carry a reverse-DNS prefix
A validator warns on a response carrying a code point the human-facing text floor excludes
requirements.gap: Python, TypeScript and .NET warn, each under HIDDEN_* and BIDI_* codes the warnings table does not name, and each checks a list narrower than the floor; Java and the reference validator report nothing (#506). With no code in the table, no suite case can ask for the warning.

requirements.statement: A renderer shows a code point the floor excludes visibly, without altering the stored value
requirements.gap: No renderer case asks how an excluded code point is presented (#110).

requirements.statement: A form is an object of version, documentType, metadata, sections, roles; structural members use native JSON types
Every defined hint member, and the expectedDataType registry; signature and file are not registered types; an unusable hint is preserved, never an error; earlier hint wins a conflict
A renderer presents an unrecognised type as text and applies hints in table order
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-117 is renderer behaviour: applying hints in the order the hints table lists them, and no renderer case asks it (#526). APR-MODEL-115 is shown by render.test.ts and EveryFieldIsAnswerableTests.

requirements.statement: No hint rejects, alters, or blocks a response
JSONC adds comments and trailing commas; duplicate keys are rejected
BCP 14 keywords are normative only in all capitals
requirements.gap: Definitional. Nothing to execute.

requirements.statement: metadata.title required non-blank; filledForm declares templateId; templateId is a URI, never fetched; workflow state is not form data; submissionUrls is an array and a scalar submissionUrl is never honoured
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-037 and 084 bind a writer, 083 a reader and 085 a validator, and no test checks them: that a writer adds no workflow member and no language, that a reader inherits a language, or that a validator never relaxes a text check for one. Both HTML renderers write lang="en" whatever metadata.language says (#524); 037 is also tracked in #434.

requirements.statement: Presentation trivia carries no meaning; everything else round-trips
At least 16 levels of section nesting
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-015 is covered by a sixteen-level vector. APR-MODEL-017 cannot be: it asks a writer to nest shallowly, and a deeper form is still valid.

requirements.statement: Attestation state never gates parsing, validation, rendering, or extraction; an attestation never authorizes reading or withholding data
requirements.gap: APR-ATTEST-053 has an example every implementation passes. The rest are reader and renderer behaviour: that a form without an attestation is ordinary, that parsing and extraction never wait on verification, and that refusing to act is a host policy rather than a format rule. A document is valid either way, so no vector distinguishes a conforming reader from one that gates.

requirements.statement: A submission entry is an https pre-signed target, as a put or a post, or a mailto address; delivery is one request or an attachment, on explicit user action, never following a redirect
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-086, 088 and 089 have no test: nothing checks that a submission sends no credentials, cookies or derived headers, refuses a redirect, and never retries on its own. Both submission paths disable redirects, but no test returns one. APR-MODEL-090 is a permission, and nothing shows it (#523). APR-MODEL-128 to 139 define the object form of an entry, the post kind, and refresh. No reader accepts an object entry yet — the reference validator and the Python SDK both report WRONG_TYPE for one — so no case can carry them and none is written, because it would fail every driver (#418). APR-MODEL-140 states the mailto attachment shape, which was prose without a keyword or a rule until now; no driver submits, so the suite cannot ask it (#523).

requirements.statement: metadata.regarding names records this form was completed against by digest; it asserts context only, and an unresolved reference leaves the document valid
requirements.gap: The array shape and digest form are gated by the schema and two executable examples. That a reader never reads a reference as revision or authority, and never rejects an unresolved one, is reader behaviour no vector asserts.

requirements.statement: vnd.apr media types name the representation; representation and document type determined by content, not name
requirements.gap: APR-SEC-005 and 007 have reader and desktop tests, and APR-SEC-012 has submission tests. APR-SEC-006, 008 and 015 are writer, host and reader behaviour around filenames that no test checks. APR-SEC-013 and 014 concern a media type arriving with a document, and no implementation reads one, so no test reaches them.

requirements.statement: Nothing a document carries executes; reading fetches nothing and contacts no submission target or certificate endpoint unasked; a reader bounds depth, refuses cleanly at a bound, and terminates
requirements.gap: APR-SEC-009, 010 and 016 are scored by renderer cases, which only the renderer drivers answer. APR-SEC-017 has no case: no renderer case carries a proof whose certificate names an endpoint. APR-SEC-011, 019 and 020 are tested in .NET, where a document nested past the reader's ceiling is refused with a parse error rather than a crash; no document vector nests past a bound, and none could fix what a conforming bound is. APR-SEC-018 is a recommendation whose bounds are implementation-defined.

requirements.statement: Sections and prompts in array order, a section's own prompts before its child sections; a renderer may paginate, group or lazily load
core is required of every implementation, each other profile is optional, and core+attestations is claimed only with core+streams
requirements.gap: The harness holds each claimed profile to every case in it and refuses a declaration claiming core+attestations without core+streams. That an implementation conforms to core is what answering the core cases shows; the optional levels are permissions nothing can violate.

requirements.statement: What core does with a stream, an attestation or an expression when it does not claim the profile that defines them
requirements.gap: APR-CONF-001 is core-only behaviour: a single-form API handed a stream must report APR_STREAM_REQUIRES_ITERATION and must not select a record by position. The harness asks whether a document was accepted, not which API was called. Reaching it needs the profile-scoped run tracked separately. APR-CONF-005 and APR-CONF-012, that an implementation not claiming core+attestations never reports a document as verified and should say attestations are present but unchecked, are about what it displays. The harness scores acceptance, not wording.

requirements.statement: A streams reader that does not claim core+attestations accepts attestation records, and a streams writer preserves them
Prompt requires id and label; label is the accessible name
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-011's corpus pair exercises case folding only, not normalization or trimming. APR-MODEL-093 relates two versions of a template, which no single document shows, and no test checks that a writer keeps ids when it reorders prompts (APR-MODEL-094) (#525).

requirements.statement: Ids are never generated unless repair is requested; generated ids derive from the title path by JCS, SHA-256 and base32, prefixed s or p, both members of a duplicate renamed, never positional
requirements.gap: No vector yet asserts the generation algorithm; a digest vector for the three worked ids belongs beside the digest fixtures.

requirements.statement: A proof's members and signing input, the one proof type, unrecognized types reported unverifiable and preserved, and a claimed signing time shown as claimed
requirements.gap: APR-ATTEST-033 and 034 have no violating example because the .NET reader accepts a proof without `type` or `value` (#517). APR-ATTEST-008 and 035 to 037 are about signing and verifying, which the harness does not score (#333). APR-ATTEST-039 to 041 are about what a renderer shows and what an implementation concludes from a claimed time.

requirements.statement: Each witness is the digest of an earlier envelope, and no witness repeats
requirements.gap: APR-ATTEST-043 has no violating example: the .NET reader accepts a repeated witness (#517).

requirements.statement: Labels as accessible names, associated help text, structural nesting, keyboard reach and completion, saving never blocked, and header association
JSONC and YAML spellings carry one semantic model; UTF-8 encoding
requirements.gap: APR-REP-002, 003 and 019 concern the byte layer, which the suite cannot carry because it holds documents as text; the encoding hazards in ParserFuzzTests cover them. No test checks that a writer omits a byte-order mark (APR-REP-018), and no vector shows a string with a forbidden code point (APR-REP-004).

requirements.statement: A response is preserved exactly on read and write
A response is always a JSON string; null coerces on read, never on write
A role states intent and never refuses input
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-025 and 026 are covered, and APR-MODEL-121 and 122 have unit tests. APR-MODEL-027, 028, 125 and 126 are reader behaviour: that a role never decides who can type, and that a reader makes roles plain, including to assistive technology. A document declaring roles is valid whether a reader honours them or ignores them. APR-MODEL-050 is reader behaviour too: showing the identifier of a role with no name.

requirements.statement: An implementation does not claim a profile without passing the corpus revision it names
requirements.gap: Within a run the harness holds a claimed profile to every case in it, so a declaration that is not answered for fails. Whether the declaration published outside the harness is honest is not machine-checkable, and APR-CONF-014, what a claim names, is checked only as far as the profiles a driver declares. Tracked in #527.

requirements.statement: Root member requiredness, domains, and defaults
Section requires id and title and at least one prompt or child section; maxRows is at least 1
A table is declared by kind and never inferred from maxRows, canAddRows or child sections
A table section carries at least one instance; prompts alone do not satisfy it
Paired JSONC and YAML streams yield the same semantic records
Independent records, no dedup, no positional selection, RFC 7464 framing; position creates no subject, revision, chronology or trust
requirements.gap: APR-STREAM-004 concerns which entry point was called: a reader asked for one form must report APR_STREAM_REQUIRES_ITERATION when handed a stream. The document suite asks every driver to read whole streams, so only the SDK unit tests reach it.

requirements.statement: A reader rejects an APR-JSONC stream in which a record is not preceded by RS
A ragged table is advisory, never invalid
A renderer presents every prompt of a ragged instance
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-101 is renderer behaviour: presenting every prompt an instance carries. No renderer case asks it (#526).

requirements.statement: Correspondence in a table is by position; the {rowId}.{columnId} id convention is recommended and carries no meaning
requirements.gap: A recommendation about id spelling. No document is wrong for ignoring it, so no vector can reach it; the editor's tests assert that the cells it creates are named {instanceId}.{columnId}.

requirements.statement: kind=table is a structural claim licensing no layout data
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-012 is a permission to present a table any way, which no document can violate because the document does not choose the presentation. APR-MODEL-013 binds a writer, and no test checks that a writer adds no layout member to a table.

requirements.statement: expectedDataType is an affordance; it never constrains a response, and degrades to text
A writer choosing a value writes its canonical form; an empty response is no selection
requirements.gap: APR-MODEL-119 binds a writer choosing a value, and APR-MODEL-120 how a reader reads an empty response. No test checks either.

requirements.statement: A document is never invalid because of what a response means
A document is valid exactly when it carries no error from the errors table, and a warning never affects validity
requirements.gap: That a validator raises no error outside the table is the absence of behaviour: every valid case in the suite would catch one invented error, but no case proves a validator has invented none.

requirements.statement: A validator reports each structural condition as an error under the code the errors table names
Constraints JSON Schema cannot express that a validator MUST enforce
requirements.gap: APR-VAL-003 and 004 concern the stage at which a reader refuses or loads a document. The suite cannot observe the stage: a parse failure and a validation failure both answer reject.

requirements.statement: A verifier reports valid, invalid, unresolved, unverifiable and witnessed each when its condition holds, independently, never unresolved as a failure, and validity apart from trust
requirements.gap: Every rule here is about what a verifier reports, and the harness scores documents rather than verification reports (#333). The .NET and Python resolvers are tested for valid, invalid, unresolved, unverifiable and witnessed; nothing checks that validity and trust are reported separately.

requirements.statement: Exact-match version rejection; no MAJOR.MINOR negotiation
APR-YAML scalars resolve by APR's own table to the JSON value space; non-finite floats are rejected; a reader uses a safe loader
requirements.gap: APR-REP-013 requires a safe loader, which no document can show: one that would exploit an unsafe loader needs a tag, which APR-REP-020 already refuses. The resolution rows (APR-REP-008 and 026 to 029) and APR-REP-012 are shown satisfied, and a wrong resolution is caught by digest rather than by a violating document.

requirements.statement: APR-YAML is well-formed YAML with string keys, and its excluded constructs are rejected
